προφήτης, ἐπ' αὐτὴν ἔρχεται τὴν ἁγίαν πόλιν, τοῦτ' ἔστι τὴν Ἱερουσαλήμ· καὶ τὰ
συμβησόμενα αὐτῇ κατὰ καιροὺς ἐκ θείας ὀργῆς προαφηγεῖται χρησίμως· ἵν' εἰδεῖεν,
ὅτι δικαιοσύνης ὑπάρχων πρύτανις ὁ τῶν ὅλων Θεὸς, μᾶλλον δὲ αὐτὸ χρῆμα
δικαιοσύνη· οὐ τὸν οἰκεῖον ἁπλῶς γεγονότα, διά γε τοῦ πεπαιδαγωγεῖσθαι νόμῳ,
τιμᾷ καὶ προσ- ίεται, καὶ φροντίδος ἀξιοῖ· δοκιμάζει δὲ μᾶλλον τὰ ἑκάστῳ
βεβιωμένα, καὶ τοῖς μὲν ἀγαθοῖς τὴν ἕξιν διανέμει τὰ ἀγαθά· ἡγεῖται δὲ ξένον καὶ
κατ' οὐδένα τρόπον αὐτῷ προσοικειούμενον τὸν τῆς φαυλότητος ἐραστὴν, κἂν εἴ
τις εἴη τυχὸν ἀγαπητὸς διὰ τοῦς πατέρας. Ὤοντο τοίνυν ἐκ πολλῆς ἄγαν ἀμαθίας
τῶν Ἰουδαίων οἱ δῆμοι, καὶ ἀνάλωτοι παντελῶς ἔσεσθαι τοῖς ἐχθροῖς, καὶ οὐδενὸς
τὸ σύμπαν ἐπι- πηδῶντος αὐτοῖς, τὸν ἠρεμαῖόν τε καὶ ἐν πολλαῖς ἅγαν εὐημερίαις
διαβιῶναι βίον, καίτοι Θεῷ προσ- κρούοντες, καὶ εἰς πολλὴν ἄγαν ἀσέβειαν
ἀπονενευ- κότες. Προσκεκυνήκασι γὰρ εἰδώλοις, καὶ ὑποκάτω δρυὸς καὶ λεύκης
ἀναθέντες ἕδη καὶ βωμοὺς τοῖς ματαίοις θυσίας προσῆγον καὶ σπονδὰς ἐπετέλουν,
τῆς ὀφειλομένης τῷ παναγίῳ Θεῷ δόξης εἰς ἅπαν ἠφειδηκότες. Καὶ γοῦν διὰ φωνῆς
Ἱερεμίου φησὶ πρὸς αὐτοὺς περὶ τῆς Ἱερουσαλήμ· "6Καὶ μὴ λέγετε ὅτι, Ναὸς Κυρίου

ἐμαντεύοντο, καὶ ἐπὶ τὸν Κύριον ἐπανεπαύοντο λέγοντες· Οὐχὶ Κύριος ἐν ἡμῖν

ἀροτριαθήσεται, καὶ Ἱερου- σαλὴμ ὡς ὀπωροφυλάκιον ἔσται, καὶ ὄρος τοῦ οἴκου ὡς

εἰωθότος φα- νερὸν αὐτοῖς ἐποίει λέγων καὶ ὁ θεσπέσιος Ἰωάννης· "6Γεννήματ'
ἐχιδνῶν, τίς ὑπέδειξεν ὑμῖν φυγεῖν ἀπὸ τῆς μελλούσης ὀργῆς; Ποιήσατε οὖν

pass_a_gloss: Tome 5. The vision of the valley of Zion. Having foretold the capture of the Egyptians, and of Assyrians and Idumaeans, the prophet comes to the holy city itself, that is, Jerusalem; and he usefully narrates beforehand the things that will befall it at times from divine wrath, so that they might know that the God of all, being president of righteousness, or rather the very thing righteousness, does not honour and admit and deem worthy of care the one who has simply become his own, through having been tutored by the Law; but rather he tests the things lived by each, and to those good in habit he distributes the good things; and he considers strange and in no way made his own the lover of baseness, even if someone should perhaps be beloved because of the fathers. So the peoples of the Jews, from very much ignorance, thought that they would be wholly uncapturable by the enemies, and, no one at all leaping upon them, would live through the quiet life and in very many prosperities, although offending God and having turned aside into very much ungodliness. For they have worshipped idols, and setting up seats and altars under oak and poplar they were bringing sacrifices to the vain things and performing libations, having wholly been sparing of the glory owed to the all-holy God. And so through the voice of Jeremiah he says to them about Jerusalem: And do not say that, It is a temple of the Lord, because unless, correcting, you correct your ways and your practices, I will also give this house like Shiloh. And again he was accusing them through Micah the prophet, saying: Her leaders judged with gifts, and her priests answered with pay, and her prophets divined with silver, and they rested upon the Lord, saying: Is not the Lord among us? Evils will not come upon us. Because of this, because of you, Zion will be ploughed like a field, and Jerusalem will be like a fruit-guard's hut, and the mountain of the house like a grove of a thicket. And that the judgment of God comes sharp against everyone accustomed to offend, the divine John too made plain to them, saying: Offspring of vipers, who showed you to flee from the coming wrath? Make then fruits worthy of the repentance, and do not think to say in yourselves that, We have Abraham as father; for I say to you that God is able from these stones to raise children to Abraham. And already [the section breaks off].
pass_b_english: Tomos 5. The vision of the valley of Zion.

Having foretold the capture of the Egyptians, the Assyrians, and the Idumeans, the prophet comes to the holy city itself, that is, Jerusalem, and usefully foretells what would befall it from time to time through divine wrath. He does this so that they might know that the God of all is the ruler of justice, or rather is justice itself. He does not honour, welcome, and care for someone simply because that person has become his own by being schooled under the law; rather, he tests what each has lived, and grants good things to those whose way of life is good, but counts the lover of wickedness a stranger and in no way his own, even if such a person should happen to be beloved for the sake of the fathers (Romans 11:28).

Out of very great ignorance, the Jewish people thought that they would be wholly beyond the reach of their enemies, and that, with no one at all attacking them, they would live out a quiet life in great prosperity, even though they were offending God and had sunk into very great ungodliness. For they worshipped idols, and setting up images and altars under oak and poplar (Hosea 4:13), they offered sacrifices and poured libations to vain things, utterly disregarding the glory owed to the all-holy God.

So through the voice of Jeremiah he says to them about Jerusalem: “And do not say, ‘It is the temple of the Lord’; for unless you thoroughly amend your ways and your practices, I will make this house like Shiloh” (Jeremiah 7:4–5; 26:6).

Again he accused them through the prophet Micah, saying: “Her rulers judged for bribes, and her priests answered for hire, and her prophets divined for silver; and they leaned on the Lord, saying, ‘Is not the Lord among us? No evil will come upon us.’ Therefore, because of you, Zion will be ploughed like a field, and Jerusalem will be like a hut for guarding fruit, and the mountain of the house like a grove in a thicket” (Micah 3:11–12).

And the inspired John also made it plain to them that God's judgment comes swiftly upon everyone who makes a habit of wrongdoing, when he said: “Brood of vipers, who warned you to flee from the wrath to come? Bear fruits, then, worthy of repentance, and do not presume to say within yourselves, ‘We have Abraham as our father’; for I tell you that God is able from these stones to raise up children to Abraham” (Matthew 3:7–9). “Even now…” (Matthew 3:10)

choices.why: πρύτανις is the one who presides; Cyril then corrects himself: God is justice itself.
The Law as tutor (compare Galatians 3:24); being schooled by it does not make anyone God's own.
ἕδος is the seat or image of a god set up beside the altars.
ἀφειδέω with the genitive: to have no regard for the glory owed to God.
The Septuagint word for the watchman's shelter in a vineyard or orchard.
